column2: The whole world is always supported by gods, Brahmins, cows, good men and good women; therefore all are held most worthy of worship.
Where they drink is a holy place — the cows themselves are Ganga and the rest. The greatness of cows has been told; now hear their treatment likewise.
In horn diseases of cows one should give oil with rock salt, cooked with paste of ginger, bala and meat, with honey.
In all earaches, oil prepared with manjishtha, hing and rock salt should be given, or again with garlic.
Bilva root, apamarga, dhataki, patala, kutaja, applied to the tooth roots, destroys the pain;
ghee cooked with substances removing toothache, Rama, is to be known as removing mouth diseases; in tongue diseases, rock salt.
Ginger, the two turmerics and triphala in throat-seizure; in heart colic, bladder colic, wind disease and consumption;
triphala mixed with ghee is praised as a drink for cows. In diarrhea one should give the two turmerics and patha;
in all belly diseases and diseases of the branches, ginger and bharngi in cough and asthma;
priyangu with salt should be given in fractures; oil removes wind; in bile, oil cooked with honey and licorice;
in phlegm, the three pungents with honey; in blood-disease, with pushta and karaja; oil, ghee and haritala should be given cooked for broken wounds.
Masha, sesame, wheat, animal milk and ghee — a ball of these with salt is this nourisher of calves;
strength-giving for those with horns; fumigation for destroying seizures: devadaru, vacha, mamsi, guggulu, hing and mustard;
this fumigation is beneficial for cows for destroying seizures and diseases. A bell should be made for cows, adorned with this incense;
with ashvagandha and sesame white; by that the cow becomes a good milker. A rejuvenative is oil-cake; one who keeps it in the house,
in the cow-dung on the fifth, always for peace should worship Shri; and Vasudeva with scents and the rest — another peace-rite is told.
On the full moon of the bright half of Ashvina one should worship Hari; Hari, Rudra, the Unborn, Sun, Shri and Agni with ghee;
having eaten curds and worshipped cows, a circumambulation of the fire should be made; one should engage bulls in a fight outside with songs and instruments.
Salt should be given to cows and a fee to Brahmins. On occasional days like the Makara (Sankranti) one should worship Vishnu with Shri;
on the platform, a lotus in the middle, in the directions the gods on the filaments: Subhadra, the Unborn, the Sun worshipped; the manyformed, the offering outside;
Kha, Vishvarupa, Siddhi, Riddhi, Shanti and Rohini; the direction-cows in the east and so on; with kushara, the Moon and Ishvara;
the world-guardians on the lotus petals, in the pots and in the fire one should offer: fuel sticks of milk-tree, mustard, unbroken rice;
a hundred each, and gold and bronze and the like one should give to a Brahmin. Cows are to be worshipped and released for peace, joined with milk and the like.
Agni said: Shalihotra told horse medicine to Sushruta; Palakapya told elephant medicine to Angaraja.
A mantra ending in "tara," mostly of fire and sky, is called Agneya; the rest is Saumya; both are praised for the cruel and gentle works respectively.
An Agneya mantra becomes Saumya, mostly ending with "namah"; a Saumya mantra becomes Agneya, joined at the end with "phat."
A mantra asleep, or only just awakened, does not give success. The sleeping time, great-armed, the waking time is the right-flowing;
for the Agneya mantra and the Saumya mantra by reversal of this; one should know the time of awakening on both days.
One should avoid mantras whose stars, signs, hated letters and the like are bad. For the benefit of gaining a kingdom, beginning with the enemy-vowel, the Kurus;
the "gopalaka kuti" (the alphabet) is declared the full script. It should be assigned by the order of stars; the last of the vowels joined with Revati;
Vela, Guru, vowels, Shona — divided by action alone; the script letters are to be known in groups, and one should assign the sixth lord and the rest.
In the script at the crossroads the name, letters and words: Siddha, Sadhya in the second, Susiddha; the others are enemies;
one should arrange the Siddha and the rest thus, even by qualities extremely siddha. A Siddha mantra for a Siddha; a Sadhya by recitation, worship, offerings and the like;
a Susiddha by meditation alone; an enemy would destroy the practitioner. A mantra abounding in bad letters is condemned by all.
Having entered by rule the initiation ending in consecration, having heard the tantra received from the teacher, one should accomplish the desired mantra.
One steady, skilled, pure, devoted, intent on recitation and meditation, accomplished, ascetic, expert, knowing the tantra, truthful,
capable of restraint and favor is called a teacher. Peaceful, self-controlled, sharp, one who has practised celibacy, eating oblation-food,
serving the teacher, accomplished and zealous is a pupil. He is to be taught — a son too, humble and wealth-giving.
One should give the mantra; in a Susiddha one should recite a thousand for the teacher. A mantra heard by chance, by trick or by force,
and a verse placed on a leaf, if it produces anything worthless... One who accomplishes a single mantra by recitation, oblation, worship and the like,
by many rites his are accomplished with little means. For one who has well perfected a single mantra nothing here is unattainable;
what to say of a man with many mantras — he is Shiva himself. A one-letter mantra is perfected by ten lakh recitations;
with increase of letters there is decrease of recitation; by that one should infer others. For mantras two or three times the seed, recitation in a garland mantra;
when the number is not stated, a hundred and eight or a thousand in recitations and so on; a tenth part of the recitation everywhere with consecration is the oblation, they know;
when the substance is not stated, ghee in the oblation; recitation by one unable everywhere; a tenth of the root mantra for the limbs and the rest of the recitation;
by recitation of the mantra with its power the mantra-deities grant desires; the practitioner is satisfied by meditation, oblation, worship and the like.
Whispering is ten times better than loud recitation; tongue-recitation hundredfold; mental is remembered as thousandfold.
Facing east or facing down one should begin mantra work; all mantras beginning with Pranava, with speech controlled, eating prescribed food;
seated one should recite the mantras, with the vision equal to deity and teacher; places should be secluded huts, temples, rivers, lakes;
for success, with gruel and cakes, or milk-food and oblation-food. The deity of the mantra should be recited on those tithis and weekdays;
on the dark eighth and fourteenth and at eclipses and the like, the practitioner. Dasra, Yama, Anala, Dhatri, Moon, Rudra, Guru, Diti,
serpents, ancestors, Bhaga, Aryaman, the cool-radiant, Tvashtri, Maruts, Indra-Agni, Mitra-Indra, Nirriti, Water,
Vishvedevas, Hrishikesha, Vayus, the lord of waters, Ajaikapad, Ahirbudhnya, Pusha — the deities of Ashvini and the rest;
Agni, the Ashvins, Uma, Nighna, Naga, Moon, Sun, Mothers, Durga, lord of directions, Krishna, Vaivasvata, Shiva;
of the fifteenth the Moon; the ancestors are tithi-deities; Hara, Durga, Guru, Vishnu, Brahma, Lakshmi, lord of wealth —
these are the lords of the weekdays from Sunday. Now the placing of the script is told: at the hair-ends and round places, on the two eyes and two ears,
two each for nose, cheeks, lips and teeth, and for the head; the letters of the five groups in the joints of arms and feet,
on both sides, back, navel and heart in order one should place; and the ya and the rest one should place in the heart; of these there are seven elements:
skin, blood, flesh, sinew, fat, marrow and semen are the elements; vasa, milk, vasaka are written, and the lords of the script:
Shrikantha, Ananta, Sukshma, Trimurti, Amareshvara, Agnisha, Bhavabhuti, Tithisha, Sthanu, Hara,
Dandisha, Bhautika, Sadyojata, Anugraheshvara, Akrura and Mahasena — these are the protecting deities.
Then Krodhisha, Chanda, Panchantaka, Shivottama, likewise Rudra and Kurma, Trinetra, Chaturanana,
Ajesha, Sharma and Sonesha, Langali and Daruka, Ardhanarishvara and Uma, Kanta, Ashadhi and Dandin,
Atri, Mona and Mesha, Lohita and Shikhi, the two Chhagalanda and Dvirandau, Mahakala and Valin,
Bhujanga and Pinaki, Khadgisha and Vaka again, Sveta, Bhrigu, Lagudisha, Aksha and Samvartaka are remembered.
One should place in order the writings of Rudra's self-powers and the rest ending with "namah." One should place the limbs; all mantras with limbs give success.
One should place these limbs beginning with the heart-line, sky and the rest. One who recites the heart and other limb mantras: "Hridayaya namah" on the heart;
Svaha on the head; then "vashat" on the crest; "hum" on armor; "vaushat" on the eyes; "phat" for the weapon — five-limbed, excluding the eyes.
For one without limbs, one should place the limb by oneself and recite a lakh; by two orders one should offer sesame to the Goddess, Lord of speech, as told.

The Goddess of script holding a rosary, pot, book and lotus would grant poetry and the rest; one should place at the beginning of action for success. Non-poet, stainless — all mantras are perfected by the Mothers.
Sunday... Saturday and Tuesday are the days; the fifth and eighth tithis; the sixth (the empty one), the Shiva and censured; the fifth and fourteenth;
the four twilights are bad; the burnt yoga signs; one, two or many bites; bitten, pierced, and cut;
no-bite and covered — bites are thus fourfold. Three bites of one or two wounds: pain, much blood;
at night, one with a foot-mark like a tortoise — bites are prompted by Yama. Touched by a diha ant, with throat swelling and pain,
with throbbing, knotted bite; with poison; or placed without poison; in a temple, empty house, anthill, garden or hollow.
